Package dyntabs.ai.decision

Class DecisionConfig

java.lang.Object
dyntabs.ai.decision.DecisionConfig
public final class DecisionConfig extends Object
Immutable settings for EasyAI.decide(...) — the cheap, probability-returning decision call.

Resolution order (first non-blank wins)

  • provider: easyai.decision.provider → easyai.provider → "openai"
  • API key: easyai.decision.api-key → easyai.api-key
  • base URL: easyai.decision.base-url → easyai.base-url
  • model: easyai.decision.model-name → "gpt-6-luna"

⚠ Read this if your chat provider is not OpenAI

A decision model is a dedicated endpoint, not a chat completion with an extra parameter. OpenAI serves it at POST {baseUrl}/decisions with its own small model. OpenAI-compatible chat providers such as Groq or DeepSeek do not implement that endpoint at all and answer 404, so "OpenAI-compatible" buys you nothing here. So unlike voice, where inheriting the chat endpoint is almost always right, here inheritance is only right when your chat provider is OpenAI.

If it is not, set both explicitly:

 easyai.decision.api-key=sk-...
 easyai.decision.base-url=https://api.openai.com/v1/

We inherit anyway rather than guessing, because a provider-level authentication or 404 error is unambiguous, whereas a library quietly swapping your endpoint is not.

Analogy: a precision instrument that needs mains power. It will accept the socket the rest of the workshop uses, but if that socket is a different voltage you must say so — the instrument is not going to guess, and a blown fuse tells you more than a silent adapter.
